_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401884733.overall: Two struggling sides meet at the WWK Arena: Augsburg (near the bottom with 9 points) are seven league games without a win under Manuel Baum, conceding at least twice in six of them and losing 5-2 at Leipzig last time, while Mainz (12th, 10 points) have lost four competitive games in a row, though they won their first three league away games and are unbeaten in five meetings with Augsburg. Augsburg miss Banks (ligament), Matsima (muscle tear), Massengo (muscle), Brackelmann (illness) and Mounie (knee), so their back three is patched up with Gouweleeuw, Keitel and Bah expected; the numbers count these absences, including about +6% on Mainz's goals for each missing regular defender. Gregoritsch, Augsburg's top scorer, is expected back in the starting side after being benched at Leipzig (Augsburg took one point from the three games he did not start), and Mainz miss Kohr until January with Silas not ready, both counted. Referee Martin Petersen's high card record (4.5 a game, +14%) is in the numbers, as is both sides' leaky recent form; with no new absences since yesterday, I keep the numbers on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already lifted by both leaky defences' recent form and counting Brackelmann, Massengo and Matsima out (Augsburg lose some goals, Mainz gain about 6% per missing defender). Gregoritsch starting again is his normal role rather than a change, and Mainz's Tietz and Becker pairing is unchanged, so I stay at 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Augsburg winning slightly more at home. Both teams are expected in a back three with wing-backs (Wolf and Behrens for Augsburg, Caci and Mwene for Mainz), which matches how they have played all season, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, already including about 14% for referee Petersen and Mainz's high recent count. Mainz's combative Kohr and Augsburg's Massengo are out, but both are on the missing list the numbers already know, so I drop yesterday's small trim; both coaches expect a game of duels between two sides under pressure, which fits the numbers, so I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.8 shots, already lifted by Augsburg's big recent volume (+20%) and Mainz's (+8%). Augsburg are expected to play on the break with Gregoritsch as the target man, and Mainz have scored only four in their four defeats, which fits their records, so I stay at 31.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with momentum adding for both (+14% Augsburg, +6% Mainz). Augsburg's reshuffled back line is already in the numbers through the missing defenders, and no new absence has been reported since yesterday, so I stay at 10.8.

401884730.overall: The 111th Nordderby: Daniel Thioune's Werder (6th, 15 points, unbeaten at home, and Thioune has just signed a contract extension) host Merlin Polzin's Hamburg (11th, 12 points, three league wins in a row, the last 3-1 against Gladbach, but weak away), and Werder have won eight of their last nine top-flight home games against Hamburg. Werder are without top creator Marco Gruell (calf; 90min reported earlier in the week that his derby place was open, and the Bundesliga's match-day predicted side still leaves him out) and Mitchell Weiser; the numbers count Weiser but not Gruell, and the predicted attack is Njinmah, Chuki and Dinkci behind Fuellkrug, the league's top scorer with nine goals, six from set pieces. Hamburg miss Remberg, Nadir, Torunarigha, Sambi Lokonga and Poulsen (Poulsen and Sambi Lokonga counted for goals), with Daka up front and Muheim, who has scored three times from distance, in midfield. Referee Florian Badstuebner's low card record (-23%) and the derby boost (+39%) are both in the numbers; confirmed XIs were not out when I wrote this, so the view keeps the morning sizes.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already taking about 12% off Hamburg for Poulsen and 3% for Sambi Lokonga, and 4% off Werder for Weiser. Gruell, Werder's main creator (two goals, six assists), is not on the numbers' list and the Bundesliga's match-day predicted side again has Njinmah and Chuki instead, so I keep -6, about 2.5 goals; Fuellkrug's set pieces keep Werder dangerous even without him.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, most of them for Werder at home against Hamburg's back three with wing-backs. Losing Gruell and Weiser costs Werder some wide play, but Njinmah's pace and Dinkci on the flanks plus Werder's set-piece focus around Fuellkrug should still win corners, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards: they add 39% for the derby but take 23% off for referee Badstuebner, who shows only 3.1 cards a game, and both sides have been booked less than usual lately (all counted). The build-up is heated, with ex-Hamburg players facing whistles, but that is the normal derby feel the numbers already add, so I stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.1 shots, lifted by Werder's strong recent volume (+20%), including 21 shots at Stuttgart, much of it built through Gruell. With Gruell out and Weiser (counted for goals only) missing on the right, Werder lose two of their main suppliers, so I keep -4, about 29.9 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with Werder's 43 on target in six games already added (+15%). Without Gruell, who set up many of those chances, Werder's openings should be fewer and less clean, while Hamburg get Daka and Muheim's long-range shooting back, which the numbers already expect, so I keep -5, about 10.3 shots on target.

401882300.overall: Córdoba (10th, 20 points, five games unbeaten and three straight home wins) host Real Oviedo (9th, 21 points), with both a step from the play-off places. Córdoba drew 3-3 at Mallorca; Diarra joins the long-term absentees, while Kevin Medina and Cristian Carracedo are back in the squad. Oviedo lost 1-2 to Girona in Raúl González's first game after Julián Calero was sacked; they are poor at home but fourth-best away. EFE now confirms Alberto Reina and Pablo Sáenz are left out along with the long-term injured Dani Calvo and Chris Ramos, all of which the numbers already take off, and Enzo Pérez returns to replace Reina. Daniel Palencia of the Basque committee referees; his slightly above-average card record is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take off Oviedo's missing Reina, Sáenz, Calvo and Chris Ramos while adding for both sides' strong recent scoring (Córdoba have scored in nine straight league games, Oviedo in ten). Reina is now confirmed out rather than doubtful, but the numbers already assumed that, and Córdoba's open style keeps the total high, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners and already add a lot for Córdoba's 48 corners in their last six. Carracedo's likely return on the right wing fits Córdoba's wide game, but Ania admits he does not know how Oviedo's new coach will set up away, so nothing firm moves it and I stay at 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.1 cards, raised for both sides' recent bookings (23 and 21 in their last six) and for referee Daniel Palencia, who averages 5.8 cards a game against a 5.3 league average. Two mid-table sides chasing the play-offs and Ania facing his old club add some edge, but that is the same picture the numbers see, so I stay at 7.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, already well above a usual game for both teams' recent shooting (95 and 103 in their last six). Raúl González wants a pressing, direct Oviedo that shot a lot from distance against Girona, and Córdoba keep attacking at home; that matches the numbers, so I stay at 31.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, boosted for both sides' accurate recent shooting. Reina's absence is already counted and Enzo Pérez comes straight back into Oviedo's midfield, while Córdoba's front line around Percan is unchanged, so I stay at 10.6.

401882298.overall: Sporting (8th, 23 points, two games without a win and over a month without a home win) host Las Palmas (11th, 20 points), three points behind them. Nicolás Larcamón is badly short: Juan Otero and Àlex Corredera are banned and Alejo Sarco and Manu Rodríguez injured (all in the numbers), and Antonio Casas, César Gelabert, Pablo García and Konrad de la Fuente are also injured, which the numbers do not know; Andrés Ferrari, back from a broken fibula, is set to start up front. Albert Sánchez's Las Palmas travel with seven absences: Opoku (banned) and most of the injured are counted, but Ale García and Cedeño are not; Herzog and Pezzolesi are back from Spain duty and Viti and Sergio Ruiz are still not in the squad. Dámaso Arcediano Monescillo is now confirmed as referee and his record is now in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already cut Sporting for Otero, Corredera and Sarco. I lean lower to about 2.1 because Sporting are also without Antonio Casas, Gelabert, Pablo García and Konrad, so the attack leans on academy players and Ferrari in his first start since March, and Las Palmas lose Ale García and Cedeño as well.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, close to both sides' recent levels. Sporting will push for the home win their fans demand, but with wide attackers like Konrad and Pablo García out that does not clearly add corners, and Las Palmas keep the same midfield of Loiodice, Kirian and Fuster, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, raised for both sides' recent bookings (21 each in their last six) and now also for referee Dámaso Arcediano Monescillo, who averages 5.7 cards a game. My earlier small lift was only for the referee, which the numbers now count, so I drop it; the tense home mood is already in the momentum figures and I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots, with a boost for Sporting's 86 shots in their last six. That form came with Casas, Gelabert and Pablo García, who are now injured on top of the counted absences, so I trim it to about 23.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. With most of Sporting's regular forwards out and a returning Ferrari short of rhythm, and Las Palmas missing Ale García too, I lower it to about 7.9.

401883109.overall: Girona (4th) and Eibar (5th) are level on 24 points, so this is a direct fight for the play-off places; Girona won 2-1 at Oviedo last time out, while Eibar have gone five league games without a win despite creating plenty. Match-day checks found no new absences: Quique Álvarez has Vanat and Asprilla back from international duty but is short at the back, with Àlex Moreno banned and Furtado, Bryan Gil and Jastin García injured (all in the numbers), plus Javi Boñar (injured) and Holmes Junior (Spain Under-18), which the numbers don't know, so Abdul Mumin is expected at left-back. Jokin Aranbarri's Eibar miss only Gift, Imanol and Bernat and plan to stay compact and break quickly; Arbilla is one yellow from a ban. Alejandro Morilla of the Navarre committee referees, and his low card record is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already add for Àlex Moreno's absence from Girona's defence and take a little off for Bryan Gil and Jastin García. I still lean slightly higher, to about 2.3, because Girona are also without Boñar and Holmes Junior and are expected to use Mumin, a centre-back, at left-back against an Eibar side Quique Álvarez calls dangerous on the counter; no match-day news changed that.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, already lifted for Eibar conceding 44 corners in their last six. Aranbarri plans to sit compact and defend his box when Girona have the ball, which fits the home-heavy split the numbers already show (5.9 to 3.5), so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards and include referee Alejandro Morilla, who averages 4.9 cards a game against a 5.3 average, a cut of about 7%. The play-off stakes and Arbilla playing on four yellows point slightly up, Morilla's calm record slightly down, and both are close to what the numbers see, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting (Eibar 91 in their last six). Girona's patched defence could give Eibar a little more, but Eibar will spend long spells defending deep while Girona's front line is close to full strength with Vanat back and Carles Pérez, Abel Ruiz and Pyshchur expected, so I stay at 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target and already count Eibar's accurate recent shooting (35 on target in six). With Girona missing Boñar and Holmes Junior on top of the counted ban, and a centre-back likely at left-back, Eibar's quick vertical attacks should find a little more, so I nudge it to about 9.4.

401883304.overall: Celta Fortuna (18th, 13 points, one win in ten) host Real Valladolid (14th, 18 points, six off the play-offs) at Balaídos in a match both sides need. Celta's reserve side play fast, open football but leak goals; centre-backs Joel López and Ribes are back from bans, Hugo Cuenca is now reported out after returning from Paraguay duty with discomfort, and Antañón is a doubt after travelling with the first team to the Bernabéu; Gavián, Somuah and Mateo Sobral are out (in the numbers). Valladolid, winners of their last two away games, miss Ojeda (banned) and Latasa (both in the numbers) plus right-back Trilli (not in the numbers), and Fran Escribá again stressed controlling the tempo against a young side. José Antonio Sánchez Villalobos referees and his high card record is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already boosting Valladolid for 14 goals in their last six and trimming them for Latasa and Ojeda. I lean slightly lower, to about 2.6, because Escribá wants a controlled game rather than an end-to-end one and Celta get two first-choice centre-backs, Joel López and Ribes, back from bans; Celta's leaky record (26 conceded) keeps the size small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already add for Valladolid's recent corners (39 in six) against a Celta side that conceded 47. Trilli's absence takes away one of Valladolid's attacking full-backs, but Alejo is a like-for-like replacement, so nothing points either way and I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.9 cards and include referee José Antonio Sánchez Villalobos, who averages 6.2 cards a game against a 5.3 average (+21%), on top of Celta's heavy recent booking. A tense game between a side in the drop zone and one chasing the play-offs fits what the numbers already see, so I stay at 7.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, already lifted for Valladolid's recent shooting (88 in six) and Celta's openness. Escribá's caution points slightly down and Celta's young, fast side slightly up, while Cuenca's absence and Antañón's doubt are too small to move it, so I stay at 27.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, boosted for Valladolid's 39 on target in their last six. Without Latasa (counted) Escribá has to find another option up front, and Celta keep their main scorer Álvaro Marín, so nothing new points either way and I stay at 9.8.

401876397.overall: Third-placed Paris FC (20 points, three behind PSG and one behind Lille) host Angers (17th, 8 points), who are winless in five and have not scored in their last three league games. Liam Rosenior has a near-complete squad: Ikoné and Sangui are out (both counted), centre-back Chergui (knee) and Adama Camara (hamstring) are doubts, and Lassine Sinayoko, who scored the winner at Auxerre, leads the line. Angers' Stéphane Gilli, Paris FC's coach until February, misses the suspended Lefort (counted) and Bané Diatta (counted) plus Oumar Pona, ill after Mali U23 duty; Sports Mole and Soccernet say striker El Ouazzani is back, while The Stats Zone still calls him a doubt. Angers are expected to sit deep, and referee Aurélien Petit (2.5 cards a game in four top-flight games) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already add a little to Paris FC's side for Lefort's absence in the Angers defence. Angers have scored only three in five and none in three, but El Ouazzani looks available again and Paris FC have conceded in their recent home games, while Sinayoko is in form; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, already trimmed because Angers have won few corners lately. Against a deep, struggling Angers side Paris FC should have long spells of pressure out wide through Kebbal, Matondo and Simon, which tends to produce corners, so I nudge it up to about 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and already take some off for Aurélien Petit, who has shown only 2.5 cards a game so far. Gilli facing the club that sacked him in February adds a little edge, but it is not a rivalry and nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots, with Paris FC doing most of the shooting, and they already add a lot for Paris FC's recent shooting and Angers' leaky last six games. Paris FC are expected to name the same attack as at Auxerre and Angers' plan to sit deep fits that picture, so I stay at 26.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Sinayoko is in form for Paris FC, while Angers have barely tested goalkeepers lately; El Ouazzani's return helps them a little, but the numbers already see both teams' trends, so I stay at 8.8.

401876401.overall: A Breton derby between Lorient (10th, 15 points) and Rennes (9th, 16 points), one point apart after ten games. Alexandre Dujeux's Lorient have beaten Rennes in each of the last six league meetings, have conceded only eight goals but scored just nine, and won 2-0 at Le Havre before the break; Isaak Touré (adductor) is confirmed out and Katseris is still missing, both counted, while reports differ on striker Ibrahima Baldé (Sports Mole says fit, The Stats Zone and But! Football Club say he may miss out) and Fadiga is back in training. Franck Haise's Rennes have lost three of their last four, conceding at least four in each of their last three away games, and are under pressure from their chairman; top scorer Estéban Lepaul (seven goals) is back from his ankle problem per Sports Mole, though The Stats Zone still lists him as a doubt, and Frankowski is out (counted). The numbers do not treat this as a derby, and referee Marc Bollengier (4.1 cards a game) is already in them. Confirmed lineups were not published when this was refreshed just before kick-off, and the pre-kick-off check found no new team news (only two match pages), so the morning view, built on several previews, stands.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, with Lorient's tight defence and the absences of Touré, Katseris and Baldé already taken off Lorient's side. Lepaul, Rennes' top scorer, looks set to return after missing the games the numbers learned from, and Rennes' away games have been wild lately, but one preview still calls him a doubt, so I lean only slightly higher, to about 2.75.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Lorient's 3-4-2-1 and Rennes' 3-5-2 both use wing-backs, which the numbers already reflect, and Rennes having to break down a compact Lorient block is how this fixture usually plays out, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards with Bollengier's record (4.1 a game) already in, but they do not flag this as a derby. Breton derbies tend to be fierce, Lorient's six-game run over Rennes adds needle and Rennes arrive under pressure from their chairman after a poor run, so I add a little, to about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots, already allowing for Lorient's quieter attack lately and Rennes' busier one. Lepaul's return would help Rennes' finishing more than their volume of shots, and Lorient's compact style is unchanged, so I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. A sharp finisher like Lepaul back alongside Dia should put a few more efforts on target, but after a month out he is not certain to start, so I nudge it up only to about 9.2.

401882804.overall: Leaders Barcelona (1st, 33 pts, three clear of Real Madrid and the league's best attack) host Villarreal (9th, 15 pts) at 14:00 on Sunday, the first of nine games in 28 days, with a Champions League trip to Sabah in Baku on Wednesday. Rodri, Xavi Espart, Pesquer and Bardghji are out (in the numbers); Flick confirmed on Saturday that Christensen is out for about two games with a muscle problem and that Cubarsí (psoas discomfort) may start on the bench, neither of which the numbers know, while Koundé, Eric García and Olmo are back and De Jong has some discomfort. Villarreal under Íñigo Pérez miss Diatta (in the numbers) plus Gerard Moreno, Foyth and Akhomach, which the numbers don't know, but their internationals came back fit after a 2-0 win over Getafe. Alejandro Hernández Hernández referees; the numbers add about 6% to cards for his record (4.9 a game).

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals, already high, with Barcelona's scoring run and the absences of Rodri and Espart counted. Flick has now confirmed Christensen is out and Cubarsí may only be on the bench, so Barcelona's centre-back pair (likely Eric García and Gerard Martín or Koundé) is thinner than the numbers know, while Villarreal's missing Foyth and Gerard Moreno roughly cancel each other out; a mild lean up to about 4.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners and already add Villarreal's high recent corner count (41 in six). Barcelona will dominate the ball with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha (fit after returning from Brazil), and Villarreal's wide men Moleiro and Buchanan are available; the defensive changes don't alter either side's approach, so I stay at 10.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards: they add Villarreal's busy recent card record (15 in six) and about 6% for referee Hernández Hernández, who shows 4.9 cards a game. The match has no derby or table edge and Renato Veiga is one booking from a ban, which may make him careful; nothing the numbers miss, so I keep 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, with both sides' recent shooting already added. Barcelona's front line of Yamal, Fermín, Raphinha and Adeyemi or Gordon is at full strength; Flick spoke about managing minutes in a nine-games-in-28-days run, but Wednesday's opponent is Sabah, so heavy rotation here is unlikely. These roughly balance, so I stay at 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, already raised for Barcelona's recent accuracy (40 on target in six). Villarreal without Gerard Moreno create a little less, while a Barcelona defence without Christensen and possibly Cubarsí may let Mikautadze in a bit more; no clear reason to move it, so 10.6.

401882800.overall: Promoted Racing (12th, 14 pts, most of them at home) host in-form Real Sociedad (5th, 22 pts) at El Sardinero on Sunday afternoon; only Real Madrid have won there this season, and Racing won 2-1 at Málaga last time out. Racing miss Mantilla, Andrés Martín and Maguette Gueye (all in the numbers), Belocian is back and top scorer Zabiri is expected to lead the line. Real Sociedad's squad list leaves out Barrenetxea, Yangel Herrera and Odriozola (all in the numbers) and includes Mamadou Sarr, whom Matarazzo called an option to start; Kubo, Óskarsson and Oyarzabal are back from international duty, with Crystal Palace away in Europe on Thursday, and returning internationals such as Aramburu could start on the bench. Manuel Orellana referees; the numbers add a lot to cards for his record (5.9 a game).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals and already take off Barrenetxea, Herrera, Andrés Martín and Gueye. Sarr's return at centre-back tightens Real Sociedad a little, while Racing's home games tend to be open with Íñigo Vicente and Zabiri; those pull both ways, so I stay at 3.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.3 corners, already trimmed for Real Sociedad's lower recent corner count. Racing attack down the wings with Íñigo Vicente, Iker Luque and Pablo García, and Real Sociedad use Guedes and Kubo wide; nothing new changes that, so I keep 11.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.1 cards, up sharply because referee Orellana (5.9 cards a game over 45 games) is counted, about +35%, on top of Racing's high recent card count (18 in six). Neither side has anyone suspended and the game has no derby or table edge, so with the referee already fully counted I stay at 7.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots and already add both sides' busy recent shooting (94 and 96 in six). Two open, attacking teams trading chances is what the numbers already show; Real Sociedad may start some returning internationals on the bench before Thursday's trip to Palace, but that is too uncertain to size, so 31.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. Zabiri and Óskarsson, both scoring regularly, are expected to play, and Oyarzabal is back in the squad, as the numbers assume; no change, 10.4.

401882801.overall: Osasuna (16th, 12 pts, one win in their last five) host bottom side Málaga (20th, 5 pts, still without a league win since promotion) at El Sadar, a relegation game both need; Arrasate's Osasuna drew 1-1 with Athletic last time and Málaga lost 1-2 at home to Racing with ten men. Osasuna's 23-man list leaves out goalkeeper Aitor Fernández, Bretones and Rockson (all in the numbers) and includes Herrando, Aimar Oroz, Del Castillo and Diego Rico, who is back after individual training and may start at left-back, with Budimir leading the line. Málaga miss the banned Aznou and the injured Rafita (in the numbers), plus centre-back Calero, which the numbers don't know (reports say a muscle overload), and the long-term absentees Lobete and Ochoa, who have been out since the summer so their absence is already in the team's recent figures; Diego Murillo is back in the squad after his knee injury. Ricardo De Burgos referees, and the numbers already take cards off for his quiet record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already give Málaga a small boost for Bretones being out. Málaga's back line is thinner than the numbers know: Aznou is banned and centre-back Calero is out of the squad, while Oroz is back to feed Budimir; Murillo's return softens that, so a small rise, about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, with both sides' recent corner counts already counted. Osasuna cross a lot from Rubén García and Raúl Moro for Budimir, and Rico's return adds another left-sided crosser, while Málaga, without a win, must come forward; nothing new points clearly either way, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards; they add Osasuna's recent cards (19 in six), take some off Málaga's quieter run and take 9% off for referee Ricardo De Burgos (3.6 a game in seven). They make no adjustment for the stakes, and a 16th-versus-20th relegation game with a winless side forced to take risks tends to be scrappy, so a small lean up, to about 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting and how much each concedes (about +11% each). Oroz's return and a patched-up Málaga defence point a little higher, but a nervy relegation game can slow things down, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, with Málaga's recent accuracy (33 on target in six) already counted. Budimir is fit and Málaga will field a reshuffled defence without Aznou and Calero, but I already give that a little through goals, so I stay at 9.6.

401879234.overall: Second-placed Brighton (22 points, six wins in their last seven league games, all with clean sheets) visit 14th-placed Hull (11 points), who are eight league games without a win but are one of four sides still unbeaten at home in the first Premier League meeting between the clubs. Jakirovic says Belloumi and Nobel Mendy are fit after the break (one preview still lists them as doubts) and Crooks is back from his ban, while Targett, Matazo, Morita and Ansah are out and Hughes is a doubt, all as the numbers assume. Brighton have Struijk, Chema and Hadjam back and Gross (new contract, 300th appearance, the league's top chance creator) in midfield; Minteh and Azeez face late fitness tests, and Mitoma, Ferguson, Yohanna and Tzimas are out and already counted. Expect Hull in a compact back five with about a third of the ball, playing direct to McBurnie, against Brighton's patient possession. Referee Peter Bankes (4.0 cards a game over 50 games, the league average) is counted, and with the morning team news matching what the numbers assumed I keep every stat where they put it.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals (Hull 1.1, Brighton 1.4), already trimming Hull a little for scoring only 6 in their last six. Brighton's run of clean sheets and Hull's narrow defeats and home draws point to a tight game, but that form is in the ratings, and Mitoma, Ferguson and Tzimas being out is already taken off Brighton; with Belloumi, Hull's main outlet, fit as assumed, I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, already adding a little for Hull's recent rise (31 corners in six). cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already adding about 39% for the derby, a little for Sam Barrott (4.1 a game in 54 games) and for United's high recent card count (16 in six). cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards, cut for both teams' quiet recent run (about -10% and -13%) and for Arena's low record on just three games. shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target, most of them in Juve's hands (6.0). Juve's expected front three is their usual one, Venezia keep Adams and Yeboah, and both sides' recent accuracy is already counted, so I stay at about 8.9.

401875047.overall: In-form Bologna (9th, four straight wins under Palladino) host bottom side Udinese (5 points, LLDLL), whom Paolo Zanetti took over this month and wants compact and hard to beat. goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, already lifted for Bologna's scoring run (+5%) and cut for Gueye. shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target, already raised for Bologna's sharp recent shooting (+16%). Orsolini and Odgaard are expected to lead the line as usual and Davis is listed to start for Udinese, so I stay at about 8.7.

401874960.overall: Sassuolo (17th, five straight defeats, 8 points) play their first game under Roberto D'Aversa, who replaced the sacked Aquilani and is expected to switch to a 4-3-3 with a focus on balance. corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. A more cautious Sassuolo might defend deeper and give Genoa more, but Genoa have won few corners lately (20 in six) and Berardi and Laurienté on the wings give Sassuolo some width of their own, so the two pull in opposite directions; I stay at about 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, with a referee record of one game that tells little. A first game under a new coach demanding more fight, near the bottom of the table, tends to bring more duels and tactical fouls; a small lean up to about 4.1.

401875545.overall: Fourth-placed Twente (24 pts, the league's best defence with 12 conceded, unbeaten at home in the league) host bottom side Willem II, who have 3 points from 12 games, a league-high 40 goals conceded and a league-low 11 scored under the returning coach Jurgen Streppel. Both have new coaches: Paulo Fonseca at Sporting, who said United are hard to read and expects his side to sit in a low block at times, and Mauricio Pochettino at United, whose first game was a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool. United are without Matheus Cunha (one-match UEFA ban for his red card against Roma), whom the numbers don't list, plus Sesko, Baleba, Ugarte and Rashford (counted); Shaw is a doubt and Zirkzee is expected to lead the line. Fonseca confirmed Ioannidis and Flavio Goncalves are fit, while Debast and Nuno Santos need a few more days (counted). Polish referee Szymon Marciniak (3.5 cards a game) is named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take Sesko off United and now list Rashford too. Cunha's ban is the one thing they don't see, and he is one of United's main attackers, so I take about 4% off, to about 2.8; Ioannidis being fit for Sporting removes the other reason I had for a bigger cut this morning.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, with United slightly more of them. Fonseca expects Sporting to defend deep at times, which could hand United more corners, but Sporting attack wide through Catamo and Araujo at home, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, already lowered about 9% for referee Marciniak's low card count and 11% for Sporting's quiet recent record, and raised 4% for United's busy one. Cunha's ban removes one hot-headed player and Bruno Fernandes' return to his old club adds a little edge, but both are small, so I stay at 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, with United's recent shot volume adding about 9% to their side. Without Cunha, one of their busiest shooters, United's attack rests on Mbeumo, Fernandes and Zirkzee, and Sporting may sit deeper at times, so I trim a little, to about 27.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, split evenly. Cunha's ban, which the numbers don't see, takes one of United's main finishers away, while Sporting have Suarez and Ioannidis fit, so I trim only slightly, to about 10.1.

401915816.overall: Kairat (27th of 36, two points from three games) host Mjällby (9th, seven points) in Almaty on matchday 4 and need a win to climb out of the elimination places after a 1-1 draw at Atalanta, under interim coach Zhora Harutyunyan, who took over when Rafael Urazbakhtin left in late October. Kairat's domestic season is over, so they come in with about three weeks without a competitive game, and their weak recent shooting and leaky defence (14 conceded in six, including 1-5 at home to Panathinaikos) are already in the numbers. Mjällby flew out on Monday via Istanbul (around nine hours in the air each way) and still have an Allsvenskan finale at Halmstad to come, where points matter after a season spent near the bottom; forward Jacob Bergström went off after 41 minutes against Malmö with a thigh problem and his place in the trip was still described as uncertain, while Dalsgaard and Stavitski (already in the numbers) stay out. Polish referee Paweł Raczkowski has now been named; his low card record (3.8 a game) is already in the numbers, so the view still leans only slightly lower on shooting.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already trim Kairat for scoring only 3 in their last six. Kairat's long break could blunt their attack but also loosen a defence that let in five at home to Panathinaikos, while a missing Bergström or a rotated Mjällby side after the long trip points slightly down, so with these pulling both ways I stay at 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners, already cutting Kairat for winning only 12 in their last six and lifting Mjällby a little for their recent 17 in three. Kairat will want to push at home, but Mjällby as the fresher, in-season side can keep the ball, which the near-even split (4.4 to 4.3) already shows, so I stay at 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, already taking a little off for referee Paweł Raczkowski (3.8 cards a game in his six games on record) and for Mjällby's tidy recent record. There is no rivalry between the clubs; a Kairat side that must win could foul more if they fall behind, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots and already take about 7% off Kairat for their low recent shooting. I trim a little more, to about 24.2, because Kairat have had no competitive game for around three weeks under an interim coach, and Mjällby may be without Bergström after his thigh injury and could rotate after the long trip with a league finale to come; the numbers can't see either.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already cutting Kairat by about 10% for only 14 on target in six and lifting Mjällby for their accurate recent shooting. Kairat's lack of match rhythm since their league season ended and the doubt over Bergström, Mjällby's main aerial threat, point a little lower, so I go to about 8.1.

401915815.overall: Ajax (11th of 36, 6 points) host FC Thun (19th, 3 points). Ajax have won six of their last seven and beat ADO Den Haag 3-0 on Sunday, but lost 18-year-old midfielder Jorthy Mokio late in that game: he has a broken fibula, has had surgery and is out until about late February, and the numbers' missing list for Ajax is empty, so they don't know. Julian Brandt, Sofyan Amrabat and Anton Gaaei are back, Bissouma is not registered for Europe, and Dolberg, Adingra and Tsygankov are long-term absences already in Ajax's form. Míchel called Thun 'the most important match' and said he is not thinking about Sunday's Klassieker at Feyenoord, so heavy rotation now looks less likely than I assumed yesterday. Thun lost 3-2 at Young Boys, miss defenders Montolio and Saiz long-term, have striker Furkan Dursun and midfielder Mattias Käit doubtful with back problems, and face three games in a week after this; no referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.2 goals, 3.2 of them for Ajax, and already add 4% for Ajax's 16 goals in their last six and Thun's leaky defence. What they can't see is Mokio's broken fibula (he scored in the 3-0 against ADO and was in the expected eleven) and Thun's main striker Dursun being doubtful; Brandt's return softens the first, so I trim 4%, to about 4.0 goals. I dropped the rotation argument because Míchel says Thun is the priority.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, 6.5 of them Ajax's, against a Thun side that usually has well under half the ball. Losing Mokio changes who plays in midfield more than how much Ajax attack down the flanks, and recent corner form on both sides is already counted. I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, with Thun expected to collect more (2.6) chasing the ball, and both sides' recent bookings are already in. No referee is named in the brief and nothing points to a heated night between two clubs with no history. I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.4 shots, about 20 of them Ajax's, and already add 3% for Ajax's recent volume (21 shots against ADO). Without Mokio and with Thun possibly missing Dursun up front, I take off 2%, to about 29.8 shots; Ajax at full strength otherwise should still dominate the ball.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target and already take about 6% off Thun for their weak recent accuracy. Thun's best finisher Dursun is a doubt and Ajax lose one of their scoring midfielders in Mokio, neither known to the numbers, so I trim 3%, to about 9.3. Thun's long-term injured defenders are already in their form.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, 8.2 of them Brighton's. Even a changed Brighton side will keep the ball and push Craiova's back three deep, which is what the numbers expect, and Craiova's low recent corner count is already in. I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, already up about 6% for referee Jöllenbeck's 5.3 cards a game and a little for both sides' recent bookings, with Craiova (2.6) expected to collect more chasing the game. Costinha's red at Hull carries a league ban only. I stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, almost 22 of them Brighton's, and already add 2% for Brighton's recent volume. A rotated side without Yalcouyé should create a little less, so I take off 3%, to about 27.9 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target and already take 8% off Brighton for poor recent accuracy, with the injured forwards counted. Rotation points slightly the same way, so I take off 2%, to about 10.3; Craiova's attack, with Al-Hamlawi fit, is unchanged.

401915810.overall: Egnatia (26th of 36, 2 points) host Lincoln Red Imps (22nd, 3 points) at the Air Albania Stadium in Tirana, still looking for a first win at this stage; the club has sold 200-lek tickets to fill the ground. Egnatia lost 1-0 at Skënderbeu at the weekend but lead the Albanian league; defender Eneo Bitri is suspended and Bakayoko has a cruciate injury, both already in the numbers, while one Turkish preview also lists Eljon Sota as injured and Ildi Gruda left out, which the numbers don't know. News was thin, and nothing in it is big enough to move the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and already add about 6% to Lincoln's side because Bitri, a regular in Egnatia's defence, is suspended. Egnatia want to attack in front of a big home crowd, but they drew tight games with Midtjylland and AGF; the absences of Sota and Gruda (one report only) and Eersteling's doubt are too uncertain to move anything. I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already move them for Lincoln conceding many (52 in their last three) and winning few. Egnatia at home with a full stadium should have more of the ball, which the numbers expect. I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, split evenly, with Egnatia's recent bookings already adding a little. Referee Oscar Johnson is named but the numbers have no card record for him, and I found nothing showing him to be strict or lenient, so I don't guess. I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots and already push Egnatia's side up about 10% and Lincoln's down 11% for recent form, as Lincoln have been outshot heavily by stronger sides. Egnatia rotate a lot, but that is in their record too. I stay at 27.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, already moved for Egnatia's better recent accuracy and Lincoln's weak attack. Beyond Bitri's ban and a couple of fringe absences there is no team news that changes the picture, so I leave it at 9.4.

401915811.overall: Hearts (32nd of 36, 1 point) host Monaco (4th, 9 points from 9) at a sold-out Tynecastle; Hearts have not won in nine European games this season and need points, while Monaco are almost through. Hearts arrive after an 8-0 win at Dundee, with Borchgrevink, Mato and Ageu back from injury and Vrancken expected to keep a similar eleven, but McEntee, Fagan-Walcott, Kingsley, Halkett, Spittal and others are still out, all in the numbers (including a big cut for McEntee). Monaco miss Golovin, Ansu Fati and Idumbo-Muzambo (counted) plus Elebi according to one team-news site; they are winless in six Ligue 1 games and go to Lyon three days later, so changes are likely. Austrian referee Daniel Schlager, around average at 4.1 cards a game, is now named and already counted. Nothing new is big enough to move the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.3 of them for Monaco; they take off for Golovin and Idumbo-Muzambo and cut Hearts' side by a quarter for McEntee. Hearts just scored eight without McEntee, which suggests that cut is generous, while a rotated Monaco side before Lyon points the other way; the two roughly cancel, so I stay at 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, split almost evenly. Hearts at home, needing a result and in scoring form, will push forward in front of a full ground, while Monaco usually have more of the ball; the numbers already capture that balance and both sides' recent corner counts. I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, already low for Monaco's few recent bookings and nudged 2% for referee Schlager, whose 4.1 cards a game is right on the average. Nothing I read points to a bad-tempered night. I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots and already take 6% off Monaco for their lower recent shot output. Hearts' confidence after the 8-0 and the returns of Borchgrevink and Mato could add a few home shots against a changed Monaco side, but that form is partly in the numbers already. I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target, 5.1 of them Monaco's, and already take 4% off Hearts for recent accuracy and count Golovin's absence. Elebi's reported absence is a defender, not a shooter, so I stay at 8.7.

401915813.overall: Iberia 1999 (29th of 36, 1 point) host Getafe (30th, 1 point) in Tbilisi; Iberia, top of the Georgian league after a 1-0 win at Samgurali, lean on striker Amiran Dzagania (15 goals this season), while Getafe need to win to keep any top-24 hope. Getafe are in trouble at home: they lost 3-0 to Atlético on Sunday, sit just above the LaLiga drop zone, and Bordalás said after the Brighton defeat that 'the Conference is already forgotten' and that league football is the priority, amid public tension with the club over squad depth. That points to a heavily changed Getafe side, more than their usual European rotation, with a LaLiga trip to Espanyol on Monday. Carvajal, Boselli, Juanmi and Uche are out and in the numbers; Romanian referee Horațiu Feșnic is named and already counted. I lean a little lower on Getafe's attack for the expected reserve side.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.7 of them for Getafe. With Bordalás openly putting the league first and a relegation fight on, a second-string Getafe side that already struggles to score away is the likely line-up, which the numbers can't see; Iberia's Dzagania keeps their side alive. I trim 5%, to about 2.6 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, more of them Getafe's, and already add a little for Getafe's high recent count. Bordalás says his squad has no real wingers, which is already in their record, and a changed side plays the same direct way. I stay at 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already high for this competition, up 9% for Iberia's recent bookings and about 5% for referee Feșnic's 5.5 cards a game. Getafe's physical style is in their record whoever plays, and Djené's red against Atlético carries a LaLiga ban only. I stay at 6.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots and already add 7% to Getafe for their recent volume. A reserve-heavy Getafe side under a coach who called the competition forgotten should create less, so I take off 4%, to about 23.9 shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target; Iberia have managed few lately and Getafe's aim has been poor, both already counted. The expected rotation weakens Getafe's attack further, so I trim 4%, to about 7.8.

401915812.overall: Lugano top the Conference League table with 9 points from 3 games (11 scored, 4 conceded), while Jablonec are 23rd on 2 points with no win yet after a 1-1 at Riga, so they need points here to stay in the race for the top 24. Lugano lost 5-0 at St. Gallen on 8 Nov after Albian Ajeti's early red card, then beat Grasshopper on 21 Nov, and they go to Lucerne in the league on Sunday, so Mattia Croci-Torti may rotate again as he did in Europe last time. The key point: on 23 Nov the Swiss league cut Ajeti's ban to two games, and both the club and RSI confirm it applies only to domestic games, so he can play in Jablonec, while the numbers take him out as suspended. Jablonec are without keeper Jan Hanus (Klemen Mihelak deputises) and Kevin-Prince Milla, both counted; captain Nemanja Tekijaski, out at Riga, is no longer on the injury list. Referee David Smajc (6.0 cards a game in a small sample) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and take about 16% off Lugano's scoring because they list Ajeti as suspended. Lugano and RSI both confirm his ban covers only Swiss league games, so he is available here; I add part of that back to about 3.3, not all of it, because Croci-Torti rotates in Europe and Ajeti may not start. Jablonec's stand-in keeper for the injured Hanus is already counted.

corners.text: The numbers expect 9.0 corners, 5.3 for Jablonec at home, and already count Lugano's slightly low recent corner count. Jablonec need a result and should push more at home than they did on the counter in the league, but Lugano dominate the ball against most sides in this group, so the two roughly cancel and I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers expect 5.2 cards and already push both sides up for recent card-heavy games (Jablonec +9%, Lugano +5%) and add about 6% for referee David Smajc's record. Ajeti's red at St. Gallen was a domestic matter and does not make this game hotter, so I stay at about 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots and already count Jablonec's recent shooting and Lugano's busy attacking in Europe. A rotated Lugano side could shoot a little less, but Ajeti's availability gives them a proven forward and Jablonec must come out at home, so I stay at about 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target and already count Lugano's sharp recent finishing (35 on target in six). Jablonec's number-three keeper situation affects goals more than shots, and Ajeti's return roughly offsets any rotation, so I stay at about 9.2.

Riga's long-term absentee Varslavans is already counted, referee Daniyar Sakhi is in the numbers, and news for this match was otherwise thin.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already cut Zalgiris for scoring only 3 in their last six. I lean slightly lower to about 2.5: both teams come in after three weeks without a competitive game, and Riga's new coach Didier Zanetti has had two days to work, which usually makes for a cautious, less fluent game; it is a mild call, not hard news.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.7 corners, 4.8 for Zalgiris at home, and already count their low recent corner count (4 in three). A new Riga coach could change the shape, but there is no word on how, so I stay at about 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.0 cards, already trimming Riga sharply (-11.5%) for only 2 cards in their last three and lifting Zalgiris slightly, with referee Daniyar Sakhi counted. The Baltic-derby billing could add some edge, but neither side has a discipline story, so I stay at about 4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots and already count Riga's busy recent shooting and Zalgiris's low output (21 shots in three). Both sides should be near full strength with no domestic games to rest players for, and the coaching change cuts either way, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target, already down for Zalgiris's 4 on target in their last three. Svedkauskas's fitness (one early-November report) matters more for goals than for shots, so I stay at about 8.4.

Referee Ishmael Barbara's low card rate is already in the numbers.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.4 corners and already add for both sides' high recent corner counts (Pafos conceded 52 in six). A rotated Midtjylland might sit deeper and give Pafos more of the ball, which could cut both ways for corners, so I stay at about 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.4 cards and already cut both sides about 9-10% for low recent card counts and referee Ishmael Barbara's 3.3 a game. shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, 12.6 for Midtjylland. I trim to about 26.8 since a rotated away side with Copenhagen on Sunday is likely to shoot less, and Pafos are without Ngamaleu, one of their wide outlets; neither the schedule nor his injury is in the numbers.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, already lifted for Pafos's sharp recent shooting (26 on target in six) and cut for Lele's ban. I lean lower to about 9.3 for likely Midtjylland rotation and Ngamaleu's injury on top of Lele's absence.

In Norway they won a wild 4-3 at KFUM on Sunday 22 Nov with Neraysho Kasanwirjo starting, which eases the knee worry reported earlier; their long injury list (Tronstad, Sorensen, Kjartansson, Gudmundsson and others) is already in the numbers. goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 1.9 for Brann at home, and already count Brann's 16 goals in six and the absences of Gudmundsson and Sorensen. I trim slightly to about 3.1 because AGF are also without midfielders Mikael Anderson and Tomas Kristjansson (one Danish preview), who are not in the numbers, and AGF have scored only once in three European games; a mild call.

corners.text: The numbers expect 11.9 corners and already add for Brann's strong recent corner count (40 in six) and cut AGF's. Brann attacking at home for a top-8 spot fits that picture rather than adding to it, so I stay at about 12.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.9 cards, 2.4 of them for AGF, and AGF's recent card rate and referee Antoniou Menelaus are already counted. AGF took just one yellow against Lyngby and there is no rivalry edge between these clubs, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots, with Brann at 18.5 and already lifted for their recent shooting and AGF's record. AGF's 20 shots against Lyngby show they can still create, which offsets their missing midfielders, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target and already lift Brann (34 on target in six) and trim AGF (8 in three). Kasanwirjo started on Sunday, so Brann look close to their usual side, and I stay at about 10.6.

401915506.overall: Besiktas (8th, 7 points) host Hapoel Be'er Sheva (33rd, 1 point) in Batumi, Georgia, because the game could not be staged safely in Istanbul; Hapoel's team manager says about 13,000 tickets have gone to Besiktas fans and around 16,000 are expected, so it should feel close to a home game, with heavy security and calls from Hapoel to avoid friction. goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, about 2.3 for Besiktas and 0.7 for Hapoel, and already lift Besiktas for 15 goals in their last 6 (+4.1%) and for Marciano's absence in Hapoel's goal (+6.2%), with Wolf deputising. Akdag's reported ban weakens Besiktas' back line a little, but with a mostly Besiktas crowd in Batumi the home edge is largely kept. I stay at about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.3 corners, 4.7 for Besiktas, already trimmed slightly for both sides' recent corner counts. Besiktas should have most of the ball against a side near the bottom of the table, and the neutral venue changes little for set pieces, so I stay at about 7.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with Hapoel the more booked side, and already take 12% off for referee Morten Krogh, who shows only 2.9 cards a game. The political tension around the fixture is real and security will be heavy, but with almost no Israeli away support and a mainly Besiktas crowd I see no clear push either way, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, 19.0 for Besiktas. With around 16,000 Turkish fans expected, losing the Istanbul crowd should cost little, and Besiktas' attack (Vlahovic, Trossard, Cerny) is scoring freely; the Galatasaray league game next could bring changes, but none are announced. I stay at about 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 on target, 7.8 for Besiktas, and already lift Besiktas for sharp recent finishing (+3.6%) and trim Hapoel's (-6.3%). A stand-in goalkeeper for Hapoel affects goals more than shots on target, and the venue change does not alter Besiktas' attack, so I stay at about 10.5.

401915519.overall: Celta (27th, 3 points) host Bournemouth (2nd, 12 points from four wins) at Balaidos. Bournemouth under Marco Rose have won nine in a row in all competitions and Evanilson has scored in five straight games, but Alex Toth, Julian Araujo and Juanlu Sanchez are out (all in the numbers' missing list), and previews expect some rotation, possibly a rest for Evanilson with Kroupi starting, before Sunday's trip to Fulham. Celta lost 2-1 at Real Madrid, have scored once at home in almost 300 minutes and Claudio Giraldez is under pressure; striker Borja Iglesias (calf) and Miguel Roman (knee) are still out and Carl Starfelt is close, none of them in the numbers' missing list, while local press expects Carreira, Hugo Alvarez and Pablo Duran to be rested with Villarreal coming on Sunday. German referee Harm Osmers books a little more than average, which the numbers count. I keep a small lean lower on goals for Celta's blunt attack and Bournemouth's likely changes up front; the rest stays with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, 1.2 for Celta and 1.8 for Bournemouth, and already trim Celta for scoring only 4 in their last 6 (-4.2%). Borja Iglesias, their main striker, is still out and not in the missing list, and Bournemouth may rest Evanilson, their in-form scorer; since much of Iglesias' absence already shows in Celta's form, I only go mildly lower, to about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, split fairly evenly. Bournemouth's direct, wide play and Celta's wing-backs both produce corners, and recent corner form is already in the numbers, so rotation on either side does not clearly change this. I stay at about 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already raised 13% for referee Harm Osmers (4.5 a game) and lowered for Bournemouth's few recent bookings. Yoel Lago's ban is for Celta's league game, not this one, and Bafode Diakite is one booking from a Europa League ban, which may make him careful; nothing suggests a heated match, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots and already raise Celta for shooting a lot lately (+8.4%), even if few go in. Rotation on both sides (Kroupi for Evanilson, fresh legs for Celta) changes faces more than volume, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 on target and already cut Celta's share for poor accuracy (-9.6%), which partly reflects playing without Iglesias. Bournemouth's forward line keeps their side up even if Evanilson rests, so I stay at about 8.8.

401915517.overall: Dinamo Zagreb (9th, 7 points) host Bayer Leverkusen (7th, 9 points) at the Maksimir, both chasing the top-eight places; Dinamo reached the knockouts with 10 points last season, so a win here would go a long way. Dinamo have won all three games under new coach Jerko Leko, most recently 3-2 against Istra, but captain Josip Misic is doubtful after a wrist knock in that game and Scott McKenna and Robert Mudrazija remain out (the latter two in the numbers' missing list); Mudrazija is also not registered for this phase. Leverkusen beat Paderborn 4-0 for a second straight league win and travel to Dortmund on Sunday, with Martin Terrier and Kennet Eichhorn still out and Guela Doue doubtful (all in the missing list). Ukrainian referee Mykola Balakin shows few cards, which the numbers already count. With the absences already known to the numbers and Misic's doubt minor for the totals, I stay with the numbers on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 2.1 of them for Leverkusen. McKenna's absence is in the missing list and has lasted a month, during which Dinamo conceded fewer than expected, and a doubt over midfielder Misic changes little in front of goal; Leverkusen's forwards are close to full strength apart from Terrier. I stay at about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.3 for Leverkusen, who have won a lot of corners lately (already counted, +1.6%). Leverkusen should have most of the ball, and Leko's Dinamo have been direct and quick in transition, which the numbers see in their recent games, so I stay at about 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards and already take 18% off for referee Mykola Balakin, who averages 2.8 a game; he has been criticised at home for not sending off a player after a dangerous tackle, which fits that record. The Maksimir crowd can raise the temperature, but that is part of Dinamo's home record, so I stay at about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.8 shots and already lift Leverkusen for heavy recent shooting (+6.4%). Leverkusen may manage minutes with Dortmund on Sunday, and Dinamo under Leko have been on the front foot, but neither clearly moves the total, so I stay at about 27.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 on target and already lift Leverkusen (+6.8%) after 45 on target in their last six. With the absences on both sides already in the missing list, I stay at about 9.9.

401915507.overall: Marseille (31st, 3 points) host Levski Sofia (10th, 7 points) at the Velodrome and need a win to keep slim knockout hopes alive. Their four-game winning run ended on Sunday with a 3-2 home defeat by promoted Le Mans after leading 2-0; Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg missed that game ill and is listed as doubtful, while Emerson and Derek Cornelius are long-term absentees already in the numbers. Levski beat Lokomotiv Sofia 4-1 at the weekend, but two Bulgarian outlets report that key midfielder Serginho (adductor strain) will miss the trip, and Radoslav Kirilov is also out; only Kirilov is in the numbers' missing list. Montenegrin referee Nikola Dabanovic books a little more than average, which the numbers count. I lean slightly lower on goals and shots on target for Levski's weakened attack.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, 2.4 for Marseille and 0.8 for Levski, and already lift Levski a little for Emerson's absence. Levski will be without Serginho, their main creator (4 goals, 8 assists), who is not in the missing list, which trims their small share; Marseille's late defensive lapses are partly in their recent record already. I go mildly lower, to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 6.9 for Marseille. Levski usually defend deep away from home, which pushes corners Marseille's way, but that is in the numbers already, as is both teams' lower recent corner count. I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, already raised 9% for referee Nikola Dabanovic (4.6 a game), lifted for Marseille's recent bookings and lowered for Levski's. A frustrated Marseille side under pressure could pick up a card or two, but nothing concrete points that way, so I stay at about 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, 18.7 for Marseille, already trimmed for their lower recent shot count (-6.9%). Marseille need the win and should have long spells of pressure, while Levski without Serginho may shoot less, but they rarely shoot much away anyway, so I stay at about 27.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 on target, 7.2 for Marseille, and already trim Marseille for poor recent accuracy (-6.8%). Levski's attack loses Serginho, which takes a little off their 2.9, so I go slightly lower, to about 9.9.

401915521.overall: Olympiacos are 6th in the Europa League with 10 points and unbeaten in five European games, after a 6-2 home win over Iraklis on Sunday; AC Milan are 28th with 3 points and Ruben Amorim has called this 'the game of a lifetime', since a defeat would leave their play-off hopes in real trouble. New since yesterday: Leon Bailey, Olympiacos' in-form winger who scored twice against Iraklis, has a hamstring strain and is out for about three weeks (sport24 and onsports both report it); he is not in the numbers' missing list. The numbers already take off Chiquinho, Hezze, Puerta, El Kaabi and Yazici for Olympiacos and Perera (banned), Gabbia, Saelemaekers, Loftus-Cheek and Chukwueze for Milan; Pavlovic is also out with kidney stones, Ramos is fit, and the Gazzetta-based line-ups have Modric and possibly Rabiot rested ahead of Cagliari on Monday. English referee Chris Kavanagh is now named; the numbers already add for his card record (about +18%), though in the Europa League he has averaged over six yellows a game. My leans are small: a touch fewer corners and shots for Olympiacos without Bailey, a touch more cards because Milan must chase.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals (1.0 Olympiacos, 1.2 Milan), already cut for Chiquinho and Hezze being out and nudged up for both sides' recent scoring. Two new things pull in opposite directions: Olympiacos lose Bailey, scorer of two on Sunday, while Milan have to win and should play with Pulisic behind a fit Ramos. With Modric likely rested on top of that, I drop yesterday's small upward lean and stay at about 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.9 corners, 5.3 for Olympiacos, already adding for their busy wide play and taking off Milan's low recent count. Bailey's hamstring strain removes one of Olympiacos' main wide outlets, which the numbers do not know, so I trim a little to about 8.6; Milan stay short of wingers with Saelemaekers and Chukwueze out, which is already in their low figure.

cards.text: The numbers now say 4.8 cards, adding about 18% for referee Chris Kavanagh's record and trimming a little for both sides' calm recent games. The referee is counted, so I don't size him again, although his Europa League average is higher still; my small lean to about 5.0 is for the stakes, with Milan needing a win in a full, loud Karaiskakis and Olympiacos chasing a top-eight place.

shots.text: The numbers expect 24.7 shots, 15.4 for Olympiacos and 9.4 for Milan, already adding for Olympiacos' busy attack and cutting Milan for their thin recent output. Olympiacos lose Bailey, their most dangerous attacker on Sunday, which the numbers cannot see, so I trim slightly to about 24.0; Milan chasing the game works the other way, which keeps the cut small.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, with Milan's lower recent accuracy already taken off. Pulisic and Ramos lead Milan's threat and both should start, while Olympiacos lack Bailey and El Kaabi but still have Gelson and Armando González; the small loss is already reflected in my shots trim, so I stay at about 8.3 here.

401915520.overall: RB Salzburg are 26th with 4 points and coach Danny Röhl says the aim is 'clearly three points' against Ararat-Armenia, who are last with no points and 14 goals conceded in four games, though they beat Van 2-1 on Friday and have lost only once in the Armenian league. Salzburg lost 1-0 at Austria Wien on Sunday, Konate missing an early penalty and the side making few clear chances after the first half-hour. Their absentees (Tabakovic, Schmid, Boma, Kitano, Mellberg, Omoregie, with Redzic doubtful) are all in the numbers, as is Ararat's banned keeper João Bravim; Morgalla is now also doubtful with a shoulder problem while captain Veratschnig is close to a return, which roughly evens out at right-back. Only about 8,000 tickets were sold, so the Red Bull Arena will be two-thirds empty. Dutch referee Lawrence Visser is named and his high card rate is already counted; I keep the numbers except a small trim to shots on target.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, 1.5 for Salzburg, already taking off Tabakovic, Redzic and Kitano and adding for Ararat playing without first-choice keeper Bravim (Nersesyan should deputise). Ararat concede plenty in Europe and Salzburg must win, but both are things the numbers already see, so I stay at about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.6 corners, 5.3 for Salzburg. Sports Mole expects Lindstrom and Vertessen on the wings with Ararat sitting deep, the pattern the numbers already assume, and losing a central striker changes who finishes moves more than how often Salzburg reach the byline, so I stay at about 8.6.

cards.text: The numbers now say 5.4 cards, adding about 27% for referee Lawrence Visser's 6.2 cards a game and a little for Ararat's busy recent card count. Both are already counted; a quiet, two-thirds-empty stadium and a side expected to dominate the ball give no reason to go higher, so I stay at about 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers expect 29.7 shots, 18.8 for Salzburg, already adding for their busy recent attack. Against a bottom side with a reserve keeper Salzburg should still have the ball and shoot often even without Tabakovic, so volume should hold and I stay at about 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, adding for Salzburg's sharp recent shooting; their missing players only change the goals number, not this one. I trim slightly to about 10.0: much of that accuracy came through Tabakovic, and without him in Vienna Salzburg made few clear chances after Konate's saved penalty.

401915508.overall: Union Saint-Gilloise are 4th in the Europa League with 10 points and top of the Belgian league after a 1-0 win at Kortrijk; they play this home game at Den Dreef in Leuven, which they are not expected to fill. Lech Poznan lead the Polish league but have only 1 point in Europe, and Niels Frederiksen wants a win here or against Ferencvaros; the squad flies in on Wednesday morning and home straight after the match. Lech are without captain and striker Mikael Ishak (hamstring, out until the winter break), Walemark, Moutinho, Gholizadeh and Douglas, all already in the numbers, and Daniel Håkans felt knee discomfort before Sunday's game but was expected to train. Union miss captain Kevin Mac Allister long-term, Biondic's knock is counted, and Massiré Sylla's absence at Kortrijk is still unexplained. Spanish referee José María Sánchez Martínez is now named and his card record is already counted; no fresh team news points either way, so I keep the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, 2.6 for Union, with Biondic's absence already taken off. Lech have been without Ishak since late October, so their recent scoring already reflects that, and Håkans should be fit; Sylla's possible absence at the back for Union is small and unconfirmed, so I stay at about 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.2 corners, already trimming Union for their low recent corner count. Lech are short of wingers with Walemark out and Håkans only just recovering, but their side is already small (3.1), so I stay at about 8.2.

cards.text: The numbers now say 4.2 cards, adding about 18% for referee Sánchez Martínez's record and lowering for both sides' calm recent games. Lech need points but are a passing side rather than a rough one, Union play a controlled game, and a half-empty Den Dreef adds little heat, so I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers expect 30.8 shots, with Union expected to dominate (21.3). Both clubs play league games three days later, but Frederiksen needs points and Union keep a settled side, so the open game the numbers assume still fits and I stay at about 31.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.6 shots on target, already adding for Union's accurate recent shooting. Union hit the woodwork and had chances at Kortrijk, and Lech's attack without Ishak is what their recent games already show, so I stay at about 11.6.

401915518.overall: Benfica top the Europa League with four wins from four, are chasing a tenth straight win in all competitions and want a top-eight place; they beat Torreense 3-1 in the Taça de Portugal on Sunday with a strong side. Viktoria Plzen are 30th with 3 points, their only European win a 1-0 over Lillestrøm, and they won 2-1 at Bohemians on Saturday. Benfica are without Leandro Barreiro (counted in the numbers), Prestianni has right-groin discomfort and per Record may need rest, and Aursnes and Banjaqui missed Sunday's game; Prestianni has started only once in Europe this season. Plzen, under Radoslav Kováč, miss defender Václav Jemelka (counted) and have Sampson Dweh back from Liberia duty. Croatian referee Igor Pajač is now named and the numbers already lower the cards for his very low card rate; with nothing new pointing either way, I keep the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.9 for Benfica, already nudged up for their scoring run and down for Barreiro. Prestianni is a doubt but has rarely started in Europe, and Pavlidis is fit; Plzen create chances at home but leak goals, which the numbers already know, so I stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers expect 8.9 corners, with Benfica pushing (5.2) and a small trim for Plzen conceding few corners lately. Benfica's wide play is the usual pattern the numbers already know, and a possible absence for Prestianni does not change that much, so I stay at about 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers now say 4.0 cards: Benfica's high recent card count adds, but referee Igor Pajač, at 2.7 cards a game, takes about 17% off. Plzen will need to stop Benfica's runners, which the numbers already assume, and the referee is counted, so I stay at about 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers expect 28.2 shots, already adding for Plzen's busy recent attack. Benfica may rotate a little after Sunday's cup tie, but Marco Silva wants to seal a top-eight place and his changed sides have kept producing, so I stay at about 28.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, already adding for both sides' accurate recent shooting. Nothing new on either attack beyond Prestianni's doubt and possible rotation, which Benfica have handled without losing output, so I stay at about 10.6.

401915504.overall: Crystal Palace (21st, 5 pts) and Real Sociedad (20th, 5 pts) are level just outside the play-off places, so both need points with two league-phase games left after this one. Palace sacked Pierre Sage last week and Thomas Frank lost his first game 3-2 at Coventry, with the club bottom of the Premier League; the numbers know nothing about the change. In Europe Palace are without Adam Wharton (red card) and Yeremy Pino (third yellow), which the numbers do not have, plus Ismaila Sarr, Chadi Riad and Takehiro Tomiyasu, while Jorgen Strand Larsen is doubtful with an ankle problem; Jean-Philippe Mateta's ban is a Premier League one. Real Sociedad miss Barrenetxea, Herrera, Odriozola and Aramburu, which the numbers count, and also Luka Sucic (illness) and Astiazaran, which they do not, with defender Mamadou Sarr doubtful. Norwegian referee Rohit Saggi (about 3.8 cards a game) is in charge and both sides play again in the league on Sunday, so some rotation is possible.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals (Palace 2.2) and already count Barrenetxea and Herrera out for Real Sociedad and Aramburu missing from their defence. They do not see that Palace lose Pino, one of their top scorers this season, and Wharton, their main passer, to UEFA bans, with Strand Larsen carrying an ankle problem, or that Sociedad lack Sucic, one of their two leading scorers. So I go lower, to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already nudged up for Real Sociedad's recent corner count (40 in six games) and for Palace conceding many lately. Losing wide players on both sides (Pino, Sarr, Barrenetxea) could trim crossing a little, but Frank's sides have usually leaned on set pieces and direct play, so nothing clearly points either way and I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already lifted for both sides' recent bookings (Palace 15 in six) and trimmed a little for referee Rohit Saggi's calm record (3.8 a game). Wharton and Pino, both recently booked or sent off, are out, but this is a tense game between two sides level on points, so I stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, with Real Sociedad's very busy recent shooting (106 in six games) already adding about 19% to their side. Palace lose two of their main creators in Pino and Wharton and Sociedad are without Sucic, none of which the numbers know, so I shade it to about 26.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, already a bit lower for Palace's quieter recent attack. With Pino and Sarr out, Strand Larsen doubtful and Sucic missing for Sociedad, the quality of chances should drop a little, so I go to about 8.9.

401915516.overall: Ferencvaros are 3rd with four wins from four, including 2-0 at AC Milan, and a win would all but secure a top-eight place; Celje are 25th with 4 points and fighting to stay in the play-off places. Balazs Borbely's side lost 3-1 at home to ETO on Saturday, ending a long unbeaten run, which he put down to unusual defensive and goalkeeping errors. Bamidele Yusuf is banned after his red card in Milan, for which he apologised publicly; the numbers already count it (about -17% on Ferencvaros's goals). Celje won 2-0 at home on Sunday with their usual starters and have no new absences beyond Pisek, who the numbers list. Italian referee Simone Sozza (about 4.1 cards a game) is in charge; news on both sides was thin and no full match preview was out yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals and already take a big slice off Ferencvaros for Yusuf's ban, with Lenny Joseph, who scored both goals in Milan, expected to lead the line. Saturday's loss to ETO showed some defensive wobbles, but Ferencvaros had conceded just 3 in their previous six, so nothing new points either way and I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already up a little because Celje have conceded 43 in their last six. Ferencvaros should have most of the ball at home, which the split (5.4 to 3.9) already shows, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards, already trimmed for both sides' calm recent card counts and set by referee Simone Sozza's average record (4.1 a game in 52 games). Yusuf's red in Milan was a one-off moment rather than a sign of a heated side, so I stay at 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.3 shots, with Celje's quieter recent shooting (49 in six) already taking 11% off their side. Celje's weekend win came with their usual starters, so no rotation is in sight, and I stay at 25.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, already raised for Ferencvaros's sharp recent finishing (31 on target in six). With no new absences found beyond Yusuf's ban, which the numbers count, I stay at 9.6.
