Omonia under Henning Berg drew 1-1 with APOEL, have Christou out and Magiabela doubtful, and one Cypriot report wondered whether Berg will put the league game first. English referee Samuel Barrott (about 4.0 cards a game) is in charge.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals (Juventus 1.9) and take only a little off for Locatelli. They do not see that Juventus will be without Yildiz, Alajbegovic and Nico Gonzalez and plan wide rotation with a new-look attack before Como, so I go lower, to about 2.6; Kalulu missing in defence and a possibly rotated Omonia keep the cut moderate.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners, mostly Juventus (8.0), already up for their 44 corners in the last six games. Omonia will defend deep, which the split already shows, but a reshuffled Juventus side without their main wide dribblers should press a little less, so I shade it to about 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already trimmed because Juventus draw few bookings lately (5 in six) and Omonia have been calm, with referee Samuel Barrott close to average (4.0 a game). A one-sided game with Omonia defending tends to stay quiet, and rotation does not change that, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots, with Omonia's recent shooting already adding about 15% to their side. A heavily rotated Juventus without Yildiz, Alajbegovic and Nico Gonzalez should create a bit less, so I go to about 29.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target, 7.6 of them for Juventus. With their main creators out and the attack reshuffled for rotation, Juventus's finishing should be a little less sharp, so I go to about 9.6.

401915501.overall: Lyon are 13th with 7 points and need a win to push toward the top eight; Lillestrom are 34th with 1 point and close to elimination. Lyon's new coach Carlos Vicens, who replaced Paulo Fonseca, won 1-0 at Lille on Saturday in his first game, built on possession and pressing; this is his first home match and the numbers know nothing about the change. The numbers count Lyon's main absences up front, Lois Openda and Pavel Sulc (Openda is reported back in training but still listed out), and Mata, Morton, Ouedraogo and Kango are also missing. Lillestrom lose Gustav Nyheim to a yellow-card ban on top of Garnas and Bassi. goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals (Lyon 1.9) and already take about 15% off Lyon for Sulc and Openda. Likely rotation before Monaco trims Lyon a little more, while Lillestrom's Nyheim ban, which the numbers do not see, slightly weakens their attack, so I shade it to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 12.0 corners, 8.1 for Lyon, already up for their 38 corners in the last six. Vicens wants possession and pressing high up, which fits a game spent in Lillestrom's half, but rotation pulls the other way, so I stay at 12.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, with referee Sebastian Gishamer close to average (4.2 a game) and both sides' recent bookings already counted. A one-sided home game rarely gets heated, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots, 19.4 of them for Lyon. A rotated Lyon side without Sulc and Openda should still dominate but a little less sharply, so I go to about 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.5 shots on target, already up for Lillestrom conceding 30 on target in six games. With Lyon's two main forwards out and changes likely before Monaco, I shade it to about 11.2.

401915505.overall: NEC (12th, 7 points) and Rennes (17th, 6 points) are both in the play-off places and a win would push either toward the top eight. NEC lost 4-1 at home to PSV on Saturday, with Dick Schreuder saying his side brought too little energy, and their defence is thin: Bram Nuytinck is out, Perr Schuurs and Geiger are doubtful, and Philippe Sandler and Deveron Fonville had problems last week; the numbers take Schuurs off on the scoring side but count none of the defensive gaps. Both sides play in the league three days later, and Serbian referee Nenad Minakovic (about 3.9 cards a game) is in charge.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and already take about 9% off NEC for Schuurs, who is in fact only doubtful. They do not see that NEC's back line is missing Nuytinck and possibly Sandler and Fonville after shipping four to PSV, so I lean a little higher, to about 3.5; Lepaul not being fully fit keeps the lean small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, already adjusted for NEC winning more corners lately (38 in six) and Rennes fewer. Nothing in the team news changes how either side builds attacks, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with referee Nenad Minakovic slightly below average (3.9 a game) and Rennes's calm recent card count already in. Both teams need the points but neither has a heated history with the other, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots, already raised for NEC's busy recent shooting (105 in six). A thin NEC defence could let Rennes shoot more, but possible rotation on both sides before the weekend pulls the other way, so I stay at 29.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. With NEC's makeshift back line likely to give Rennes cleaner chances, I lean slightly higher, to about 10.7.

401915503.overall: OFI Crete (16th, 6 pts) host Anderlecht (15th, 6 pts) in Heraklion, a straight fight for a play-off place between two sides on two wins from four. OFI arrive after a 0-2 home defeat to Panathinaikos and have a long injury list: striker Kenan Kodro, defender Kresimir Krizmanic, midfielders Fotis Koutsoupias and Konstantinos Lagoudakis, plus Chnaris and Marinakis; the numbers already count these. Anderlecht are unbeaten in four and won 1-0 at OH Leuven, where goalkeeper Colin Coosemans (foot) and striker Sikan played through knocks; they are without Lucas Hey and possibly Ilay Camara, both on the numbers' list, and travel on Wednesday despite a Greek general strike. Estonian referee Kristo Tohver, who has shown about 5.3 cards a game in his few matches on file, is in charge, which the numbers already count.
